intro: B2: conflicts in an apartment block, renting or buying, getting a deposit back. We learn to negotiate and argue a choice.
speaking.0.promptUa: Describe the illustration. Say what the conflict is about and how you think the neighbours should resolve it. Also say which rules of living together in an apartment block you consider most important.
speaking.0.phrases.0.ua: One can assume that the conflict concerns…
speaking.0.phrases.1.ua: In my opinion they should first talk calmly.
speaking.0.phrases.2.ua: In an apartment block the most important things are… and…
speaking.0.phrases.3.ua: If talking doesn't help, one can…
speaking.0.tips.0: **Don't judge** the conflict — analyse it: «wygląda na…», «prawdopodobnie nie wie, że…». That is B2 interpretation.
speaking.0.tips.1: The structure «zamiast + infinitive» («zamiast wzywać policję») is precise and elegant.
speaking.0.tips.2: **Cisza nocna** — quiet hours at night (in Poland usually 22:00–6:00, according to the building's rules).
speaking.1.promptUa: Is it better nowadays to rent a flat or to buy one with a mortgage? State your opinion, justify it and explain what you think about the opposing arguments.
speaking.1.phrases.0.ua: In the present situation renting seems more sensible to me.
speaking.1.phrases.2.ua: Of course I understand the supporters of buying, who…
speaking.1.phrases.3.ua: To sum up, the choice depends on…
speaking.1.tips.0: **Płacąc czynsz, …** — an adverbial participle (-ąc) at the start: a neat B2 device, like «Decydując się…».
speaking.1.tips.1: Give an example «Znam rodzinę, która…» — it's a quick argument from experience, even a generalised one.
speaking.1.tips.2: Finish with a condition: «zanim podpiszemy…, warto…» — practical advice sounds convincing.
speaking.2.promptUa: You have moved out of a rented flat, but the owner doesn't want to return the whole deposit. You are talking to him on the phone. Defend your position and try to reach an agreement.
speaking.2.phrases.0.ua: According to the contract I should receive it within…
speaking.2.phrases.1.ua: I don't agree with this claim.
speaking.2.phrases.2.ua: I have evidence: photos and a handover record.
speaking.2.phrases.3.ua: I would like us to put this in writing.
speaking.2.tips.0: **Normalne zużycie ≠ szkoda** (normal wear ≠ damage) — the key legal argument in deposit disputes.
speaking.2.tips.1: Always propose a **written agreement** («na piśmie») — that is what makes negotiations effective.
speaking.2.tips.2: Keep a polite tone even in a dispute: «Jeśli ma Pan…, chętnie go zobaczę».
writing.0.promptUa: You are looking for a flatmate for a two-room flat. Write an advert for a portal: describe the flat and the area, state the monthly cost, name your expectations of a flatmate and how to get in touch.
writing.0.phrases.0.ua: A separate room with a balcony is at your disposal.
writing.0.phrases.1.ua: The monthly cost is… including bills.
writing.0.phrases.2.ua: I'm looking for a calm and responsible person.
writing.0.phrases.3.ua: Interested people, please get in touch.
writing.0.tips.0: An advert — **concise and specific**: floor area, district, price, what's included, who you're looking for.
writing.0.tips.1: **Wraz z opłatami** — «including bills»: critical information for any tenant.
writing.1.promptUa: For several months renovation has been going on in the neighbouring flat, starting as early as seven a.m., also at weekends. Write a formal letter to the building manager: describe the problem and its effects, recall the rules, propose a solution and say what further steps you will take if nothing changes.
writing.1.phrases.0.ua: I'm writing about the nuisance noise…
writing.1.phrases.3.ua: If the situation doesn't improve, I will be forced to…
writing.1.tips.0: A formal complaint: **facts → consequences → basis (regulations) → demand → consequence for the other party**. Five paragraphs — five points.
writing.1.tips.1: **Wnoszę o + accusative** — purely formal «I request/petition for» — appropriate in letters to institutions.
writing.1.tips.2: Don't threaten — **inform about the steps**: «będę zmuszona zwrócić się…» — a professional tone.
listening.0.intro: A radio interview with a real-estate market analyst.
grammar.0.intro: B2: conditional sentences, relative pronouns, causal constructions.
grammar.0.questions.0.why: **gdyby** + past-tense form (był): «gdyby czynsz był niższy»; «by» is already part of «gdyby».
grammar.0.questions.2.why: **chyba że** = «unless»: an exception. «Dlatego że» — a reason.
grammar.0.questions.4.why: **być zobowiązanym do + genitive** — the formal construction «obliged to…».
